questions.q: What is quant hiring typically looking for in a resume bullet, more than most other technical fields?
options: The widest possible breadth of unrelated technologies listed
Evidence of rigor — a precisely stated hypothesis, an honest test of it, and awareness of where the result is weak
The single highest performance number achievable, regardless of method
A long list of certifications with no project detail
questions.explain: Quant hiring emphasizes rigor and intellectual honesty — interviewers who have built and broken strategies themselves are quick to spot an oversold claim.

questions.q: Which capstone bullet best follows the pattern this lesson recommends?
options: "Built a profitable trading strategy using machine learning."

"Researched and backtested a dollar-neutral cross-sectional reversal strategy across 11 sector ETFs using Ridge regression and purged walk-forward validation; net Sharpe 0.42 after realistic cost modeling."
"Created a guaranteed-return algorithm ready for live trading."
"Worked on some quant stuff involving ETFs."
questions.explain: The strong version names the specific method (Ridge regression, purged walk-forward validation) and reports an honestly-qualified net result rather than an unqualified or inflated claim.

questions.q: What belongs in a quant portfolio beyond the resume itself?
options: Only a polished README with the headline Sharpe ratio and no other detail
A reviewable repository including the data pipeline, validation code, cost model, and full performance report with its limitations section intact
A list of job titles with no code or methodology
A single screenshot of a profit chart
questions.explain: A portfolio should let a reviewer verify resume claims directly, including the limitations section — a reviewer trusts bullets far more when the caveats haven't been stripped out.

questions.q: What should NOT change when tailoring a resume to a specific job posting?
options: The order in which skills and bullets are presented
Which project is emphasized first
The underlying substance — never add a tool, library, or result you can't discuss for five minutes under questioning
The length of the summary section
questions.explain: Tailoring means reordering genuinely relevant content to match a posting's emphasis, not fabricating skills or claiming familiarity with tools you can't defend in an interview.

questions.q: In the recommended one-page structure, why does the education section carry more weight for quant roles than in many other technical fields?
options: Because quant firms never look at project work
Because quant hiring still weighs math and CS fundamentals (statistics, linear algebra, stochastic calculus) heavily alongside applied project work
Because GPA is the only factor quant firms consider
Because education is listed last and therefore ignored
questions.explain: Quant hiring, more than most technical fields, still weighs the math and CS fundamentals shown in coursework and degree, alongside the capstone and experience sections.
